planting.note: Best started from leaf-pulling divisions or offsets after the winter rest, and most hobbyists keep it in a terrarium or humidity tray rather than an open garden bed.

directions: This Oaxacan species forms a summer rosette of sticky, glandular leaves that trap small insects, then contracts into a tight, non-carnivorous succulent-leaved rosette to ride out the dry winter. Keep the mineral-rich, fast-draining substrate consistently moist and humidity high during active growth, flowering with slender stalks bearing small pink to lavender blooms. Reduce watering sharply once the winter rosette forms, letting the mix dry further between waterings until new carnivorous leaves resume in spring. Grows well alongside other Mexican Pinguicula in bright, indirect light with protection from intense direct sun.
sources: International Carnivorous Plant Society (ICPS) Pinguicula species pages
